prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but “best” depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and whether this is an insurance job. If you want, give me your Miami ZIP code and whether the roof is residential or commercial and I’ll pull a short list of top-rated contractors near you and vet them for hurricane-rated work.

Meanwhile, here’s what to look for and how to find the best hurricane-rated roof replacement contractor in Miami:

Key qualifications and certifications (must-haves)
- Miami‑Dade County NOA-compliant systems: Contractor must install materials/systems that have a Miami‑Dade County Notice of Acceptance (NOA) for HVHZ (High Velocity Hurricane Zone) use. Ask to see the specific NOA numbers for the materials they plan to use.  
- Florida license & insurance: Verify the contractor is a Florida Certified Roofing Contractor and carries general liability and workers’ compensation insurance (get policy numbers and call carrier to confirm).  
- Manufacturer certifications: Preferred contractors / Master Elite status from shingle or metal manufacturers (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, TAMKO, etc.) — this helps ensure material warranty and installer training.  
- Experience with HVHZ details: Proven experience installing hurricane clips/straps, code-compliant fastening schedules, correct flashings, self-adhering underlayment in critical areas, and uplift calculations.  
- Local references and portfolio: Ask for recent Miami/Dade jobs (photos), and contactable homeowner references for outages during hurricanes.  
- Written, transferable warranties: Manufacturer warranty plus an installer workmanship warranty in writing (length and whether it’s transferable).  

How to verify
- Florida DBPR license lookup (construction license).  
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control NOA search (verify materials).  
- Better Business Bureau, Google/Nextdoor reviews, and ask for recent local references.  
- Ask to see permits pulled and final inspections on previous jobs.

Practical process tips
- Get at least 3 detailed written estimates. Compare not just price but scope: number of layers removed, underlayment type, nail type & spacing, deck repair allowances, flashings, ventilation, removal & disposal, permit & inspection handling, schedule, payment schedule, lien waivers.  
- Require the contractor to pull permits and obtain final inspection.  
- Avoid large upfront payments; typical deposits are 10–30% with progress payments and final payment on completion and final lien waiver.  
- For insurance claims: get a contractor experienced with insurance adjusters and able to provide a scope and Xactimate-style estimate if needed.

Materials & design considerations for hurricanes
- Class 4 impact-resistant shingles or metal roofing are common in Miami for better wind and impact performance.  
- Correct roof deck attachment and continuous load path (clips/straps) required for HVHZ.  
- Proper flashings, self-adhering underlayment at eaves and rakes, and sealed penetrations.  
- Good attic ventilation and insulation to reduce uplift risk and improve shingle life.

Cost ballpark (very general)
- Asphalt shingles (HVHZ-rated/impact-resistant): often $5–12+ per sq ft total installed.  
- Metal roofing: typically $10–25+ per sq ft.  
- Tile: $12–30+ per sq ft. (depends on tile type, deck reinforcement).  
Prices vary widely by home, pitch, access, tear-off complexity and scope.

Sample questions to ask a contractor
- Are the materials and system you propose Miami‑Dade NOA-approved for HVHZ use? Show the NOA.  
- What is your Florida roofing license number and insurance policy numbers?  
- Do you carry workers’ comp for your crew?  
- How many Miami‑Dade hurricane-rated roofs have you installed in the past 12 months? Can I see references/pictures?  
- What exact materials, underlayment, fasteners and flashing details will you use? Provide a written scope.  
- What warranties are provided (manufacturer + workmanship) and are they transferable?  
- Who pulls the permit and who is responsible for final inspection and corrections?

If you’d like, provide your ZIP code and whether the project is residential or commercial and I’ll research and shortlist 3–5 highly rated Miami-area roofing contractors experienced with hurricane-rated replacements and show how they match the criteria above.
